migration.description: Advance existing committed reservation ceilings during bounded background preparation; preserve the deployed allocator protocol.

durable_state.description: Existing conversation and UTC-hour namespace rows and last_invoke_sequence ceilings. Prepared ranges are private memory issuance rights until their reservation transaction commits.
durable_state.storage_implementation: Existing SQLite tables and existing pending journal identity obligations.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: Supported v4.8.x and v4.9.0 implementations of the current/standby 64-ID reservation protocol.
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Runtime recovery candidate; version chosen by repository release policy.

dml_changes.description: Reserve at most 64 IDs per owner in the existing transaction and compare-and-update the previous ceiling. Publish issuance rights only after commit and native settlement. Startup reads at most 4096 covering activity entries and 128 owner keys within the shared two-second background seed budget; it does not recreate removed conversations. Current UTC-hour preparation and final-60-second next-hour preparation use the existing namespace allocator. Actual missing-range demand takes priority over evictable speculative preparation.

progress_signals: cvm_runtime_recovery_diagnostics_total fixed invocation_range reasons distinguish initialization, admission, refill, exhaustion and preparation outcomes.
cvm_invocation_range_phase_duration_seconds separates cache admission, write admission, connection and transaction time.
pause_points: Between preparation turns and between committed reservations; startup and HTTP readiness do not await preparation.

recovery.program_rollback_state_behavior: does-not-automatically-reverse-compensate-or-down-migrate; supported earlier v4.8 and v4.9.0 readers recognize all written rows and skip committed reserved tails after restart
recovery.faulty_release_recovery: Forward repair re-enters the existing ceiling protocol. A cancelled caller does not cancel the native settlement owner. An uncommitted reservation rolls back before write admission is released; an uncertain committed tail is skipped rather than reissued. Ended-hour memory retirement retains namespace protection while active leases or journal obligations exist.

required_test_evidence: Existing durable ceilings are readable without schema migration; restart never reissues a committed range.
Concurrent same-owner demand remains singleflight; prepared memory issues under a short writer block while a new empty owner retains the 100ms boundary.
Removed seed owners do not recreate rows or starve remaining preparation; bounded activity and owner queries retain the intended index plans.
Cancelling a reservation or its finish waiter retains logical admission and the physical SQLite lock until the native owner drains.
Ended-hour eviction waits for both active lease and pending journal identity acknowledgement.

validation.evidence_scope: The committed reservation SQL, durable encoding, preparation loop, native settlement and schema retain the protocol verified by the passed integrated candidate a7b6bff0627475ed34311eef25bc988c7e3f58c0. The subsequent missing-owner handoff correction only removes an empty memory generation and notifies demand; it performs no durable mutation. Its gated regression still requires current-head CI. Component compatibility does not substitute for the parent PR's current-head CI, contention acceptance or formal review.
